audience.persona: the owner: saw the redesign explainer v4, decides the v5 reviews' open calls after watching

stake.loses_what: v5 is not ready to build: both adversaries say not converged

video.promise: By the end, you can name what the two reviews found, what each finding would need, what to buy, and the calls that are yours.
video.thesis_mechanism: Each step leaves a marker that stays valid until its pin moves: the code tree, the diff, or an event it depends on.

predecessor.name: the v4 explainer's design (pipeline-redesign v4), which v5 revised
predecessor.how_shaped_differently: v5 keys each marker by a pin per fact class instead of the head

running_example.scenario: one slice's recipe, broken and fixed once per finding in chapters 2 and 3

invariants: CI passes on the merged tree.
A verdict counts only at its exact diff.
simplifications: Shows three pin kinds (tree, diff, event); v5's fourth, the item pin, is left out.
non_scope: opus B6 and B8 (not in either joint finding or the single-finding chapter)

beats.spoken: Before anyone builds version five, two adversaries tried to break it, apart: one with the web, one who knew versions one to four. Is it ready, and what should we build or buy?

visual.assertion: Two reviews before anyone builds v5

cues.target: rail:v5 draft, two reviews, ready yet?

beats.spoken: Each step leaves a marker that stays valid until its pin moves: the code tree, the diff, or an event it depends on.

visual.assertion: A marker stays valid until its pin moves

beats.spoken: Eight blockers from one, six from the other. Both say not converged, not ready yet, and both call every blocker a specification fix, not an architectural one.

visual.assertion: Both say not converged yet

contested.fallback: Eight blockers from one, six from the other. Both say not converged, not ready yet, and both call version five a real improvement.
contested.why: 'None architectural' is vc's verdict only; opus calls B8's services unbuildable as written (OP:226)

beats.spoken: The orphan trap alarms on a valid marker the entry never reached. After a clean merge-up, the entry returns at the CI wait, short of the owner's approval, and the trap fires. Five hundred and twenty of nine hundred and ninety-nine runs merged up.

visual.assertion: A wait returns before the trap's check

beats.spoken: The integrator proposes one reviewer's fix: alarm only on a marker the entry passed and skipped, never one past where it stopped to wait.

visual.assertion: Alarm only on markers passed and skipped

beats.spoken: Git's patch-id, a hash of the diff, ignores whitespace. A fixer re-indents a permissions block: CI goes stale with the tree, but the patch-id holds, so the adversary's verdict still counts.

visual.assertion: Patch-id ignores whitespace

beats.spoken: The integrator proposes to pin its own hash of the verbatim diff, whitespace kept.

visual.assertion: Pin a hash of the verbatim diff

beats.spoken: A revert moves the parent's pin, but the child checks only a digest of the parent's result, which has not changed. So its claim is still granted against a parent gone from main.

visual.assertion: A revert leaves the child's claim granted

contested.fallback: After a revert, both reviewers find the child's claim still granted against a parent gone from main. One blames the digest check; the other says the pin never moves.
contested.why: vc: the pin moves and the digest compare misses it (VC:74-81); opus: an ordinary revert never moves the pin (OP:166-169). They agree only on the outcome

beats.spoken: The integrator proposes: compare pins, not digests, and spot a revert by its metadata.

visual.assertion: Compare pins; spot reverts by metadata

beats.spoken: A contract-path claim keeps a shared file to one item. It releases at park, when CI first goes green, before review, so a second item can take the file mid-fix.

visual.assertion: The path claim releases before review

contested.fallback: A contract-path claim keeps a shared file to one item. It can release at park, which may come before review, so a second item could take the file mid-fix.
contested.why: opus reads 'park' two ways and shows the release only under one (OP:197-207); vc reads it as worktree park (VC:128-133)

beats.spoken: The integrator proposes to release the path only when the item lands or is abandoned.

visual.assertion: Release the path when the item lands

beats.spoken: First, from one reviewer: GitHub's merge call checks only the pull request's head, so if main moves first, an untested tree lands. The owner's call: keep the API merge, check main's tree after, and treat a mismatch as main red.

visual.assertion: Merging checks only the head

contested.fallback: First, from one reviewer: GitHub's merge call checks only the pull request's head, so a moved main could land an untested tree. The other rates this landing shape as holding. The owner's call: keep the API merge, check main's tree after, and treat a mismatch as main red.
contested.why: vc rates the landing-shape fork 'Holds' (VC:184); opus's B2 says shape (b) cannot keep I1 (OP:80-98)

beats.spoken: Second, after a clean rebase, a check run on the old commit is deduped, leaving the new head without its required check. The integrator proposes keying commit effects by the tree.

visual.assertion: A clean rebase drops the check run

beats.spoken: Third, from the other reviewer: milestone one's shadow gate compares events that only arrive at milestone two. The integrator proposes moving the event log into milestone one.

visual.assertion: M1's gate needs M2's events

beats.spoken: Fourth, a rules change sends no event, so a newly required check is never read; under a bypass token, a candidate lands without it. The integrator proposes an event source per pin, or a time limit.

visual.assertion: A rules change sends no event

beats.spoken: Every workflow engine [memoizes](/mˈɛmoʊˌaɪzᵻz/) per run, by position or step id; none invalidates by fact and pin, and Shepherd already replays from the top. So both keep the core built: no Temporal, DBOS, Restate or [Inngest](/ˈɪnʤɛst/).

visual.assertion: Engines memoize per run; v5 needs pins

beats.spoken: Five edges are worth buying. First, the merge queue: GitHub's own if the repos move to an organization, else Mergify or Trunk, else our own with fast-forward.

visual.assertion: Build the core, buy five edges

cues.target: edge:merge queue|buy if eligible|GitHub, SaaS, own

contested.fallback: Five edges are worth buying. First, the merge queue: GitHub's own if the repos qualify; one reviewer would try a hosted queue next; else our own.
contested.why: opus verified the native queue only for org-owned public repos or GHEC (OP:385, 394-395), and so did the integrator (AS:186); Mergify and Trunk are opus's picks only

beats.spoken: Second, webhooks through a free tunnel, leaving the reconciler as a backstop. Third, Litestream to copy the one store.

visual.assertion: Webhooks and backups are bought

beats.spoken: Fourth, the hashes behind the pins: git gives the verbatim diff and tree hashes, and small libraries do the rest. Fifth, a lint that keeps recipes deterministic, and an eval grader.

visual.assertion: Hashes, a lint and a grader are bought

contested.fallback: Fourth, the hashes behind the pins: git gives the verbatim diff and tree hashes, and small libraries do the rest. Fifth, one reviewer would buy a lint that keeps recipes deterministic, the other an eval grader.
contested.why: The determinism lint is opus's pick only (OP:456); the eval grader is vc's only (VC:212-213)

beats.spoken: Two parts stay built. Claims and pools: Kubernetes schedulers run only on Kubernetes. The event bus: a second store would split the marker's transactions.

visual.assertion: Claims and the bus stay built

beats.spoken: Two design calls are yours. Twelve: should every version bump re-run open work, safe but costly? Thirteen: should a verdict carry to an identical diff, whitespace counted, never for a visual approval?

visual.assertion: Two design calls are yours

beats.spoken: Three more stay yours: where the repos live, for GitHub's queue; a webhook tunnel; and a backup target. Each touches an outside account.

visual.assertion: Three account calls stay yours

beats.spoken: Version six is being written to answer both reviews, and another adversary round follows. Until you decide, each fix is a proposal.

visual.assertion: Fixes are proposals until you decide

contested.fallback: Version six will be written to answer both reviews, and another adversary round follows. Until you decide, each fix is a proposal.
contested.why: v6's status at render time is unverified

A01.claim: v5 had no adversary round when two adversaries reviewed it apart: opus with the web, vc after reviewing v1-v4; neither read the other

A02.claim: The marker key is (item, fact, pin), the pin chosen per fact class (tree, diff, observed, item); CI facts take the tree pin, review facts the diff pin

A03.claim: opus: 8 blocking items, not converged; v5 is a real improvement on v4

A04.claim: vc: not converged, 6 blocking items, each a specification fix, none architectural

A05.claim: The orphan trap alarms on a valid marker the entry did not visit; after a clean merge-up the entry returns at the CI wait, short of the owner's approval, and the trap fires

A07.claim: The integrator proposes vc's call-site definition: an orphan is a valid marker the entry passed and skipped, never one beyond where it stopped

A08.claim: Git's patch-id ignores whitespace unless --verbatim; a re-indented permissions block changes the tree, not the patch-id, so a diff-pinned verdict still counts

A09.claim: The integrator proposes its own SHA-256 over a canonical verbatim diff, whitespace kept, as the diff pin

A10.claim: vc: a revert moves the parent's pin, not the digest of its projection, so the child's claim is still granted; opus: an ordinary revert never moves the pin

A11.claim: The integrator proposes both fixes: validity compares pins, not digests, and Reverted fires on revert metadata

A12.claim: A contract-path claim keeps a shared path to one item and releases at park; under one reading of park that is the first green CI, before review

A13.claim: The integrator proposes releasing the path only at the landing result or abandonment

A14.claim: opus B2: GitHub's merge call checks only the PR head, so a moved main can land an untested tree; the owner's call keeps the API merge, checks main's tree after, and treats a mismatch as main red

A15.claim: opus B4: after a clean rebase, commit-attached effects are deduped and the new head is left bare; the integrator proposes keying commit effects by the tree pin

A16.claim: vc V5-B5: M1's gate needs events that only M2's event log produces; the integrator proposes moving the event log into M1

A17.claim: vc V5-B2: observed pins have no guaranteed emitter; under a bypass, a stale land-rules marker is the only check; the integrator proposes a producer per kind or a TTL pin

A18.claim: Durable-workflow engines memoize per run by position or step id; none invalidates by fact and pin; Shepherd already replays from the top; both reviews keep the core built

A19.claim: Merge queue: native where eligible (org-owned public repos or GHEC), else Mergify or Trunk (opus), else an own fast-forward queue

A20.claim: Webhooks through a free tunnel make the reconciler a backstop; Litestream (Apache-2.0, beta badge) replicates the one store

A21.claim: Hashing parts are bought (git, canonical JSON, cacache); a determinism lint (opus) and an eval grader (vc)

A22.claim: Claims and pools stay built (Kueue and Volcano are Kubernetes-only); the bus stays in the one store, sharing transactions with markers

A23.claim: Q12: every bump invalidates, fail-safe but re-running open reviews; Q13: a verdict counts at an identical diff, with whitespace and visual approvals excluded as proposals

A24.claim: The owner keeps external accounts; the queue's home, a webhook tunnel and a backup target are new calls

A25.claim: A v6 integrator answers both reviews, then a v6 adversary round follows
